title: Traditional Turkish Bread
description: Soft, slightly chewy, and baked to a golden finish with a traditional sesame and nigella seed topping.

method.instruction: Make the pre-ferment: In a bowl, combine 225g flour, 145ml lukewarm water, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp yeast. Mix until smooth. Cover and let rest at room temperature for 2-3 hours, or refrigerate overnight.
Make the main dough: In a large bowl, combine 240g flour, 1 tsp salt, remaining yeast, and enzyme-active soya flour or malt powder (if using).
Add the pre-ferment (all of it), 165ml lukewarm water, and olive oil.
Mix until a rough dough forms, then knead for 8-10 minutes by hand (or 6-7 minutes in a stand mixer) until smooth, soft, and elastic.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and let rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide into 2 equal portions (approximately 400g each).
Shape each portion into a ball, cover, and let rest for 10 minutes to relax the gluten.
On a lightly floured surface, roll or stretch each ball into an oval or round shape, about 25-30cm long and 1-1.5cm thick.
Place shaped breads on lined baking trays. Using your fingertips, gently dimple the surface all over to create the characteristic texture.
Cover and let rise for 20-30 minutes until slightly puffy.
Brush the tops lightly with water or olive oil. Sprinkle generously with sesame seeds and nigella seeds.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden brown with a soft interior and slightly crisp exterior.
Cool on a wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes.title: Pre-ferment Benefits
notes.content: The pre-ferment (poolish) develops flavor and creates a softer, more open crumb. It's worth the extra time!

notes.title: Nigella Seeds
notes.content: Nigella seeds (black onion seeds) are strongly recommended for authentic Turkish flavor and visual appeal. They add a subtle, slightly bitter, onion-like taste.

notes.title: Flour Choice
notes.content: Laucke Mulgara Baker's flour is recommended for its protein content and performance, but any quality baker's flour will work.

notes.title: Serving Suggestion
notes.content: Perfect for kebabs, doner wraps, or torn and served alongside dips like hummus, baba ganoush, or labneh.
